intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech by wandering the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then stay for the magical transformation at dusk when food stalls fill the air with smoke and spices. Explore the labyrinthine souks of the surrounding medina, bargaining for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Journey to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga and embark on a sunset camel trek into the Sahara. Spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, sip mint tea, and wake before dawn to witness a spectacular desert sunrise over the dunes.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local chef in a riad kitchen for a hands-on cooking class where you learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as lamb tagine with preserved lemon, harira soup, and honey-drenched pastilla. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to source fresh ingredients like ras el hanout, saffron, and argan oil before cooking and dining together.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into the grandeur of Moroccan imperial history with a self-guided or locally led tour of the 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellige tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. Continue to the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden necropolis of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty rediscovered in 1917, featuring stunning marble and stucco craftsmanship.

experiences.name: Ksar of Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley Drive
experiences.description: Travel through the dramatic Atlas Mountain passes to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou, a stunning example of southern Moroccan earthen clay architecture and a famous film location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue into the lush Draa Valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, date palm oases, and Berber villages, stopping for a traditional lunch of mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) at a local auberge.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Late night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Take a petit taxi from Marrakech Menara Airport to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat (approx. 15–20 min, ~70–100 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit and settling in.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Hotel Aday by approximately 23:15–23:30. If hungry, grab a quick snack from a nearby 24-hour hanout (corner shop) on the edge of the medina. Hydrate, unpack essentials, and get a good night's sleep to prepare for full days ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A – Arrival night
meals.lunch: N/A – On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Quick snack from a local hanout (corner shop) near the hotel – bread, olives, or packaged biscuits for under 20 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Keep small change (MAD) ready for the taxi. Negotiate the taxi fare before getting in or insist on the meter. Hotel Aday is a well-known budget riad in the heart of the medina – staff are used to late arrivals. Save energy for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café (msemen flatbread, argan oil, honey, mint tea). Then walk 5 minutes to the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere – orange juice vendors, snake charmers setting up, and locals commuting. Explore the surrounding souks: Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Épices (spice market), and Souk Cherratine (leather). Bargain respectfully – start at 40% of the asking price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD) – a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan architecture, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. Afterward, walk to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and browse the historic Mellah market. Stop by Place des Ferblantiers to see lantern craftsmen at work.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at sunset – the square transforms into a massive open-air food festival. Watch storytellers, musicians, and acrobats. Eat dinner at the food stalls (numbered stalls – stall 14 and 32 are popular). Try harira soup, merguez sandwiches, and kefta skewers.

meals.breakfast: Café near Hotel Aday – msemen, honey, argan oil, mint tea (~30–40 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap local snack lunch in the souks – a bowl of harira soup and khobz bread from a street vendor (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls – harira, merguez, kefta, fresh orange juice (~60–80 MAD total)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the medina is entirely pedestrian and the alleyways are uneven. Keep your bag in front of you in crowded souks. The Bahia Palace is closed on Fridays. Carry a water bottle – March can be warm during the day (~18–22°C).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims – free) to see the iconic 12th-century minaret at its most photogenic in the morning light. Then head to the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entrance ~70 MAD), one of the most beautiful Islamic schools in North Africa, featuring intricate zellige tilework, carved stucco, and cedar woodwork. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Marrakech Museum (housed in the Dar Menebhi Palace, ~50 MAD) adjacent to the madrasa – exhibits on Moroccan art, history, and culture. Afterward, visit the Almoravid Koubba (the only surviving Almoravid structure in Marrakech, ~20 MAD). Take a leisurely walk through the northern medina neighborhoods and discover hidden fondouks (old merchant inns).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Rue Bab Doukkala area for a local neighborhood dinner experience. Try a small family-run restaurant serving a full Moroccan set menu (tajine, salad, bread, dessert). Alternatively, pick up street food from a local grill near the medina walls. End the evening with a stroll along the lit-up ramparts near Bab Doukkala gate.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a café near Ben Youssef – coffee and beghrir (Moroccan pancakes with honey, ~25–35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap local eatery in the medina near the madrasa – chicken tajine with bread (~50–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Family-run restaurant near Bab Doukkala – full Moroccan set menu (~70–90 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Youssef Madrasa and Marrakech Museum offer a combo ticket – ask at the entrance to save money. Photography inside the madrasa is permitted. This is a culturally rich day – consider bringing a small notebook to jot down impressions. Dress modestly when visiting religious and historic sites (shoulders and knees covered).

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 06:00–07:00) on a shared budget CTM bus or a pre-booked shared minivan transfer toward Ouarzazate and then Merzouga (Sahara). This is a long travel day (~9–10 hours total with stops). The route passes through the stunning High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at Aït Benhaddou – a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the ksar on foot (entrance ~10 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') – brief stop to see the Taourirt Kasbah from the outside. Continue through the Draa Valley, passing palm groves, kasbahs, and desert landscapes. Arrive in Merzouga village (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) by late afternoon (~17:00–18:00). Check into a budget desert camp or guesthouse in Merzouga.
day_by_day.evening: Mount a camel at sunset for a 45–60 minute ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes (negotiate price: ~150–200 MAD per person for a basic camel ride). Watch the sunset over the Sahara from the top of a dune – one of Morocco's most breathtaking experiences. Spend the night at a budget desert camp with a Berber dinner, traditional music around a campfire, and stargazing under an unpolluted sky.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure in Marrakech – café au lait and a msemen (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop at Aït Benhaddou – tagine or sandwich at a local café (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included Berber dinner at the desert camp – harira, couscous or tajine, mint tea, fresh fruit (~included in camp fee or ~80–100 MAD if separate)

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared transfer in advance from Marrakech (budget option: ~200–300 MAD per person in a shared grand taxi or minivan). Budget desert camps in Merzouga cost approximately 200–350 MAD per person including dinner and breakfast. Bring a warm layer – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech. Bring cash as ATMs are scarce in Merzouga.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (~06:00) to climb the nearest dune and watch the sunrise over the Sahara – an unmissable, magical experience. Take photos, meditate, or simply absorb the silence of the desert. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast (mint tea, bread, olive oil, honey, amlou almond paste). Explore the Merzouga village on foot – visit the local market, chat with Berber families, and see the small lake (Dayet Srji) nearby which attracts flamingos in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional budget activities: rent a sandboard from the camp (~50 MAD) and try sandboarding down the dunes. Alternatively, visit a local Gnawa musician's home for an informal music session (tip-based, ~20–30 MAD). Begin the return journey toward Marrakech by shared transport, stopping in Tinghir to see the spectacular Todra Gorge – dramatic 300m-high limestone canyon walls with a river running through. Walk through the gorge (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stop in Ouarzazate or continue toward Marrakech depending on transport schedule. If stopping in Ouarzazate, check into a budget guesthouse (~150–200 MAD). Explore the town center, visit a local café, and enjoy a quiet evening. If returning directly to Marrakech, arrive late evening and rest at Hotel Aday.

meals.breakfast: Included Berber breakfast at desert camp – mint tea, bread, honey, olive oil, amlou
meals.lunch: Roadside café in Tinghir near Todra Gorge – tajine or omelette with bread (~50–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Ouarzazate or Marrakech – vegetable couscous or chicken tajine (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the morning light but still beautiful in the afternoon. Wear sturdy shoes for walking in the gorge – the path can be slippery near the river. If you have flexibility, spending an extra night in the desert is highly recommended. Coordinate your return transport with your camp host the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Back in Marrakech. Rest and recover from the desert journey. After a leisurely breakfast, visit the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) – a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring intricate Italian Carrara marble and cedar carvings. Arrive early as queues form quickly. Afterward, explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) – a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mellah's historic synagogue (Beth El Synagogue – free or small donation) to understand Marrakech's multicultural Jewish heritage. Then head to the Cyber Park Arsat Moulay Abdeslam (free entry) – a peaceful garden with free Wi-Fi, popular with local students. Great for relaxing and people-watching. Browse the fixed-price Ensemble Artisanal cooperative shop (no bargaining needed) to understand fair prices for Moroccan crafts before buying souvenirs in the souks.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class or simply enjoy a final deep dive into Marrakech's food scene. Head to the Mellah market for fresh produce, olives, and preserved lemons. For dinner, try a local workers' restaurant (restaurant populaire) near the medina – these serve enormous portions of Moroccan home cooking at rock-bottom prices. End the evening with a traditional hammam experience at Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a local neighborhood hammam (~15–30 MAD for a basic hammam, ~50–80 MAD with kessa scrub).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café – coffee, khobz bread, olive oil, and amlou (~30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Restaurant populaire (workers' lunch spot) near the medina – full plate of couscous or tajine with bread (~35–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Slightly nicer budget restaurant in the medina for a farewell Moroccan feast – pastilla (pigeon pie) or lamb tajine with prunes (~80–100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Saadian Tombs and El Badi Palace are close to each other – combine them in one morning walk. The hammam is a quintessential Moroccan cultural experience – go to a local neighborhood hammam rather than a tourist one to save money and get an authentic experience. Bring flip-flops and a change of clothes. Saturday is a busy market day in the medina – great for atmosphere but watch your belongings.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Visit the Majorelle Garden (entrance ~150 MAD – the priciest attraction but worth it) – a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden created by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Also houses the Berber Museum (included in ticket). Arrive right at opening time (08:00) to avoid crowds. Alternatively, if budget is tight, enjoy the free Menara Gardens (~2km from the medina) with its olive groves and iconic pavilion reflected in a large pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the medina for final souvenir shopping in the souks – argan oil, spices, leather goods, babouche slippers, and Berber jewelry make great budget gifts. Use your knowledge of fair prices from the Ensemble Artisanal visit to bargain confidently. Enjoy a final mint tea with a shopkeeper (a Moroccan tradition). Pack your bags at Hotel Aday and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final sunset view from a rooftop café overlooking Djemaa el-Fna (café au lait or fresh juice, ~20–30 MAD). Take a petit taxi to Marrakech Menara Airport (~70–100 MAD). Reflect on an incredible week of culture, desert, history, and food in Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at a medina café – msemen, honey, argan oil, mint tea (~35–40 MAD)
meals.lunch: Quick and delicious street food lunch in the souks – makouda (potato fritters) sandwich or a bowl of bissara (fava bean soup) with olive oil and cumin (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport or early dinner before departure – or a final bowl of harira and chebakia (honey pastry) from a medina stall (~25–35 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Majorelle Garden sells out of timed entry slots – book online in advance at jardinmajorelle.com to guarantee entry and save queuing time. If skipping Majorelle due to budget, the Menara Gardens are equally peaceful and completely free. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep some MAD for the taxi and any last-minute purchases. Tip your hotel staff if they were helpful – 20–50 MAD is appreciated.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store on Rue Riad Zitoun el Kedim, or ask the hotel for a late-night snack option.

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival simple. Confirm your hotel has 24-hour reception for late check-in. Exchange some currency at the airport (aim for 500–1000 MAD for initial expenses). Avoid negotiating with unofficial taxi drivers at the airport — use the metered petit taxis or a pre-booked transfer.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast, begin exploring the heart of Marrakech. Walk to Jemaa el-Fna Square (5-minute walk from hotel) to soak in the morning atmosphere — orange juice vendors, storytellers, and snake charmers. Then head into the Souks of Marrakech: explore Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Épices (spice market), and Souk Cherratine (leather goods). Spend 2–3 hours wandering and browsing without pressure to buy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (~15 MAD entry), one of Morocco's most stunning examples of Islamic architecture with intricate zellige tilework and carved stucco. Afterward, explore the nearby Musée de Marrakech housed in a 19th-century palace (~50 MAD entry). End the afternoon with a stroll through the Mouassine neighborhood to admire its ornate fountains and hidden riads.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna Square at dusk when it transforms into a massive open-air food festival. Watch the acrobats, musicians, and Gnawa performers. Dine at one of the rooftop terraces overlooking the square for an iconic Marrakech experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Aday or a nearby café — try msemen (Moroccan flatbread) with argan oil and honey, plus mint tea (~30–50 MAD).
meals.lunch: Café des Épices near the spice market — a mid-range rooftop café with tagines, salads, and fresh juices (~80–120 MAD per person).
meals.dinner: Eat at the food stalls of Jemaa el-Fna — try harira soup (10 MAD), merguez sandwiches (20 MAD), and grilled kefta. Budget ~60–100 MAD for a full meal. Alternatively, Restaurant Chez Lamine for slow-cooked mechoui lamb (~120–150 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina's narrow alleys are uneven. Keep a small amount of cash handy for souk browsing. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price. Stay hydrated as March can still be warm during the day (~18–22°C).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring beautifully decorated mausoleums. Then walk to the Kasbah Mosque area and explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) with its distinctive wrought-iron balconies and the Lazama Synagogue. Continue to the El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD entry) — a vast 16th-century palace complex with sunken gardens and stork nests atop the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Bahia Palace (~70 MAD entry), a stunning 19th-century palace with elaborately painted ceilings, mosaic floors, and lush courtyards — one of the finest examples of Moroccan craftsmanship. Afterward, browse the artisan workshops along Rue Riad Zitoun el Jedid for quality souvenirs at fairer prices than the main souks.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Moroccan hammam experience at a mid-range hammam such as Hammam de la Rose or Hammam Dar el-Bacha (~150–250 MAD for a full scrub and massage). This is a deeply cultural and relaxing experience. Afterward, enjoy a quiet dinner in the Mellah neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near the hotel — café au lait, khobz bread with olive oil and amlou (almond-argan paste) (~40 MAD).
meals.lunch: Nomad Restaurant near the Spice Square — modern Moroccan cuisine with a rooftop view, tagines and couscous (~100–150 MAD per person).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Al Fassia Gueliz or a local darija restaurant in the Mellah — try pastilla (pigeon pie), lamb tagine with prunes, and bastilla au lait for dessert (~150–200 MAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance or go early afternoon to avoid crowds. The Bahia Palace is best visited in the morning light but afternoon works well too. Carry your entry tickets — some sites are clustered and a combined visit saves time. Photography is restricted inside some palaces.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (7:00–8:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a private or shared day-tour to the Ouarzazate and Draa Valley region, or begin the longer journey toward Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes). For a 7-day trip, take a 2-day/1-night Sahara excursion. Hire a private driver or join a group tour (~800–1200 MAD per person for a shared tour). Drive through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) with stunning Atlas Mountain scenery and Berber villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ouarzazate (~3.5 hours from Marrakech) — the 'Hollywood of Africa.' Visit the Kasbah Taourirt, a UNESCO-listed earthen fortress (~20 MAD entry), and the nearby Atlas Film Studios where Lawrence of Arabia and Gladiator were filmed (~80 MAD entry). Continue driving southeast through the Draa Valley, passing ancient kasbahs, palm oases, and rose-growing villages (the region is famous for its rose harvest in May).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your desert camp near Zagora or continue toward M'Hamid el Ghizlane for a more authentic experience. Check into a mid-range desert camp with private Berber tents (~400–600 MAD per person including dinner and breakfast). Watch the sunset over the dunes, then enjoy a camel ride (~100–150 MAD for 30–45 minutes) as the sky turns golden.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — pack some snacks and water for the road.
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside restaurant in Aït Benhaddou or Ouarzazate — try a simple tagine or couscous with local Berber bread (~80–100 MAD).
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — harira soup, tagine, couscous, and Moroccan sweets served under the stars with live Gnawa music (~included in camp price or ~150 MAD separately).

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara tour/driver at least 2–3 days in advance. Bring warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Pack sunscreen, sunglasses, a scarf (for sand), and a power bank. The drive to Merzouga (Erg Chebbi) is longer (~9–10 hours) but offers the most iconic dunes — consider whether the 2-day excursion fits your pace.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 6:30 AM) for a magical sunrise over the Sahara dunes — one of the most memorable experiences in Morocco. Climb the nearest dune for panoramic views. After breakfast at the camp, explore the surrounding desert on foot or by 4x4 quad bike (~150–200 MAD for 1 hour). Visit a local nomadic family if your guide arranges it — a genuine cultural exchange.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey to Marrakech. Stop at the UNESCO World Heritage site of Aït Benhaddou (~20 MAD entry) — a spectacular fortified ksar (village) that has appeared in Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and The Mummy. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring its labyrinthine alleys and towers. Continue driving back through the Atlas Mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening (~7:00–8:00 PM). Rest at Hotel Aday, freshen up, and enjoy a relaxed dinner in the Medina. Reflect on the desert experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast included at the desert camp — Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, eggs, and mint tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — tagine and fresh salad (~80–100 MAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range riad restaurant in Marrakech — try Riad Yima or a similar spot for home-style Moroccan cooking (~120–160 MAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is long (~4–5 hours from Zagora). Use the journey to nap or enjoy the scenery. If you extended to Merzouga, the return is a full day's drive — consider an overnight stop in Ouarzazate. Keep your camera ready on the mountain pass — the views are spectacular in afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: A slower, recovery morning after the desert journey. Visit the Majorelle Garden (~150 MAD entry, or ~200 MAD including the Berber Museum inside) — a stunning botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. The cobalt-blue villa and exotic plants are iconic. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Afterward, visit the nearby Yves Saint Laurent Museum (~80 MAD) for a fascinating look at fashion and Moroccan inspiration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gueliz neighborhood (New City) — a more relaxed, European-influenced district with art galleries, boutiques, and cafés. Visit the Marrakech Museum of Photography and Visual Arts if open, or browse the Ensemble Artisanal (government-run craft cooperative) for fixed-price quality souvenirs — great for last-minute shopping without bargaining pressure. Stroll along Avenue Mohammed V.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell Marrakech evening with a special dinner at a traditional riad restaurant. Consider a cooking class or a visit to a local family for a home-cooked meal (bookable through your hotel, ~300–400 MAD including the experience). End the night with a final walk through Jemaa el-Fna to soak in the atmosphere one last time.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Gueliz — try Grand Café de la Poste for a classic colonial-era atmosphere with croissants and café au lait (~60–80 MAD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café du Livre in Gueliz — a relaxed bookshop-café with sandwiches, salads, and Moroccan dishes (~100–130 MAD).
meals.dinner: Special dinner at Dar Yacout or a similar mid-range riad restaurant — a full Moroccan feast with pastilla, tagine, couscous, and live music (~200–300 MAD per person). Book in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden gets very crowded after 10:30 AM — arrive right at opening. The Berber Museum inside is worth the extra entry fee. Gueliz is a 20-minute walk or short taxi ride from the Medina. Saturday is a lively market day — the Mellah market is particularly vibrant in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (non-Muslims cannot enter the mosque but the gardens and exterior are beautiful and free). The 12th-century minaret is the model for the Giralda in Seville and the Hassan Tower in Rabat — a masterpiece of Almohad architecture. Stroll through the adjacent Cyber Park for a peaceful green space. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks or pick up Moroccan argan oil, spices, or leather goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the Medina. Visit the Musée Tiskiwin (~30 MAD) — a small but fascinating private museum tracing the trans-Saharan trade route through art and artifacts, very close to the hotel. Pack, check out, and arrange your airport transfer (allow 45–60 minutes to the airport, more during busy periods).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Marrakech with memories of ancient medinas, golden dunes, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday or a nearby café — msemen, beghrir (honeycomb pancakes), argan oil, and mint tea (~40–60 MAD).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near Jemaa el-Fna — Moroccan salads, brochettes, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~60–80 MAD). Keep it light before travel.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight — if time allows before departure, grab a final snack of Moroccan pastries (chebakia, ghriba) from a local bakery to enjoy at the airport (~20–30 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time carefully and plan your hotel checkout accordingly. Most hotels offer luggage storage if you have a late flight. Tip your hotel staff if service was good (20–50 MAD is appreciated). Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if required. The Marrakech airport is relatively small — arrive 2 hours before international flights.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30. Private airport transfer arranged with a luxury chauffeur service to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony and a light late-night snack prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival (22:30). Check in to Hotel Aday, freshen up, and enjoy the hotel's curated welcome amenities — traditional pastries, argan oil toiletries, and a chilled bottle of Moroccan rosé or fresh juice. Rest and prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome spread at Hotel Aday: Moroccan briouats, olives, fresh bread, honey, and herbal tea arranged by the hotel upon request

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with Hotel Aday. Keep Day 1 light — no sightseeing. The Medina streets near Derb Sidi Bouloukat can be narrow; ensure the driver knows the nearest vehicle drop-off point.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel rooftop. At 10:00, begin a private guided walking tour of the Marrakech Medina — explore the labyrinthine souks of Souk Semmarine and Souk El Attarine, visit the historic Medersa Ben Youssef (one of North Africa's finest Islamic colleges), and discover the ancient Almoravid Koubba. Your private guide will provide rich historical context throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (14th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture) followed by a stop at the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the ornate Saadian Tombs — royal necropolis dating to the 16th century. Afterward, enjoy a private hammam and spa experience at a premium riad spa near the Medina for full relaxation and cultural immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Djemaa el-Fna square at dusk to witness the magical transformation — snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians fill the square. Dine at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the square for a cinematic Marrakech experience.

meals.breakfast: Rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday: msemen (Moroccan flatbread), amlou (argan oil and almond spread), fresh orange juice, mint tea, soft-boiled eggs, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Derb Aarjan, near Rahba Kedima) — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views; try the lamb pastilla and harira soup
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Jardin (Mouassine neighborhood) — elegant garden restaurant set in a 16th-century riad; signature dishes include slow-cooked lamb tagine and bastilla au pigeon

day_by_day.notes: Book Medersa Ben Youssef and Saadian Tombs tickets in advance to avoid queues. The private hammam session should be pre-booked — recommended: Hammam de la Rose or Les Bains de Marrakech. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, depart by private luxury 4x4 vehicle toward the Ourika Valley in the Atlas Mountains (approximately 1 hour from Marrakech). Explore the lush Berber villages, terraced gardens, and the cascading Setti Fatma waterfalls. Engage with a local Berber family for an authentic cultural exchange — learn about traditional weaving and mountain life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return toward Marrakech and stop at the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum (Jardin Majorelle) — a cobalt-blue botanical masterpiece once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the Islamic Art Museum of Marrakech within the garden complex. Afterward, visit the nearby Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech for a world-class fashion and art experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Medina for an exclusive private cooking class at a premium riad kitchen — learn to prepare a traditional Moroccan feast: harira soup, chicken bastilla, lamb tagine with preserved lemon, and orange blossom pastilla for dessert. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional Berber restaurant in Ourika Valley — freshly baked bread from a clay oven, Berber omelette, mountain honey, and mint tea with panoramic Atlas views
meals.dinner: Private cooking class dinner at a premium riad — multi-course Moroccan feast you prepare yourself with a master chef; paired with Moroccan wines or fresh juices

day_by_day.notes: The Ourika Valley road can be winding — motion sickness tablets recommended if sensitive. Majorelle Garden is very popular; arrive early afternoon to avoid peak crowds. The private cooking class should be booked in advance — recommended providers: La Maison Arabe Cooking School or Souk Cuisine.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure at 07:00 by private luxury 4x4 for the epic journey to the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dunes — approximately 8–9 hours with scenic stops). Cross the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m altitude) through the High Atlas Mountains with breathtaking panoramic views. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou — a magnificent 11th-century ksar (fortified village) used as a filming location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Valley of Roses (Dadès Valley) and the dramatic Gorges du Dadès — towering red rock formations carved by ancient rivers. Stop for photos and a brief walk through the gorge. Continue through the Draa Valley's palm groves and kasbahs toward Merzouga.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga at sunset. Mount private camels (or opt for a 4x4 dune buggy) for a guided sunset ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the tallest dunes in Morocco reaching 150m. Arrive at your exclusive luxury desert camp for a night under the Saharan stars.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast prepared by Hotel Aday before departure — Moroccan pastries, fruit, and thermos of mint tea for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — traditional Moroccan tagine, fresh salads, and Berber bread baked in a clay oven
meals.dinner: Exclusive dinner at the luxury desert camp — traditional Moroccan feast served under the stars: harira, mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), couscous with seven vegetables, and Moroccan pastries; live Gnawa music and drumming performance around the campfire

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — depart early. Ensure the private driver is experienced with mountain roads. Aït Benhaddou entry fee is minimal but a guide is recommended. Luxury desert camp recommendation: Scarabeo Camp or Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp — pre-book well in advance. Pack warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring a headlamp, sunscreen, and a scarf for sand.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (05:30) for a private guided sunrise hike to the top of the highest Erg Chebbi dune — witness one of the world's most spectacular sunrises as golden light floods the endless sea of sand. Return to camp for a lavish Saharan breakfast. Explore the surrounding desert on foot or by camel, visit a local nomadic Berber family encampment, and learn about traditional desert life, navigation by stars, and medicinal desert plants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the desert camp and journey toward the Todra Gorge — dramatic 300m-high limestone canyon walls. Take a guided walk through the narrow gorge floor where a cool river runs between the towering cliffs. Continue toward Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa' — and visit the Atlas Film Studios, the world's largest film studio, where Lawrence of Arabia, Babel, and many others were filmed.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a luxury kasbah hotel in Ouarzazate (recommended: Dar Ahlam or Ksar Char-Bagh). Enjoy a sunset aperitif on the terrace overlooking the Draa Valley. Dine at the hotel's gourmet restaurant for a refined evening.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Saharan breakfast at the desert camp — fresh bread, honey, argan oil, Berber omelette, dates, fresh fruit, and mint tea served in the open desert
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant near Todra Gorge — grilled kefta, Moroccan salads, and fresh-squeezed orange juice with gorge views
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner at your luxury kasbah hotel in Ouarzazate — refined Moroccan-French fusion cuisine; signature dishes may include pigeon pastilla, lamb with prunes and almonds, and saffron crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise dune climb is steep — wear closed-toe shoes. Todra Gorge is best visited in the afternoon when light enters the canyon. Atlas Film Studios tours run throughout the day — no advance booking required but a private guide enhances the experience. Ouarzazate luxury accommodation must be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Ouarzazate — explore the Taourirt Kasbah, a stunning 19th-century fortified palace and UNESCO heritage site once belonging to the powerful Glaoui clan. Wander through the adjacent ksar village still inhabited by local families. Visit the Ouarzazate Museum of Cinema for fascinating behind-the-scenes history of the region's film legacy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Ouarzazate and return to Marrakech via the scenic Tizi n'Tichka pass (approximately 4 hours). Stop at artisan cooperatives along the route to browse and purchase premium Moroccan crafts — hand-knotted Berber rugs, silver jewelry, and fossils. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Check back in to Hotel Aday and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner experience at one of Marrakech's most celebrated restaurants — a multi-course tasting menu in a beautifully restored 17th-century riad setting with live Andalusian music. End the evening with a nightcap at a rooftop bar overlooking the illuminated Koutoubia Mosque.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the luxury kasbah hotel in Ouarzazate — full spread including Moroccan pancakes, fresh juices, local cheeses, and pastries
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop at a scenic mountain restaurant on the Tizi n'Tichka pass — hearty Berber tagine and fresh mountain bread
meals.dinner: Premium tasting menu dinner at La Maison Arabe or Dar Yacout, Marrakech — iconic riad dining experience with courses including bastilla, mechoui, and traditional Moroccan desserts; wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Taourirt Kasbah is a short walk from the town center. The return drive over Tizi n'Tichka is stunning but winding — allow extra time. Dar Yacout and La Maison Arabe require advance reservations — book at least 2–3 weeks ahead. The Koutoubia Mosque is beautifully lit at night and visible from many rooftop bars in the Medina.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins — a once-magnificent 16th-century palace described as the 'eighth wonder of the world,' now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with resident storks. Explore the adjacent Mellah market for last-minute premium souvenirs: saffron, argan oil, rose water, and hand-crafted leather goods from the famous Chouara Tannery viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a final luxury spa afternoon at a premium hammam — full traditional hammam ritual with black soap, kessa exfoliation, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Recommended: Hammam de la Rose or Royal Mansour Spa (day access). Return to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. If the flight is late evening, enjoy a final sunset dinner at a rooftop restaurant near Djemaa el-Fna — savoring last views of the Koutoubia minaret and the Atlas Mountains on the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent breakfast at Hotel Aday — full traditional Moroccan spread with fresh-squeezed orange juice, msemen, honey, amlou, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices (Rahba Kedima square) — relaxed rooftop setting with views over the spice market; try the zaalouk, kefta sandwich, and fresh lemonade with orange blossom
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Terrasse des Épices or Kechmara — elegant rooftop dining with panoramic Medina views; order the slow-cooked lamb shank, Moroccan mezze platter, and traditional mint tea ceremony to close the trip

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in — Marrakech Menara Airport can be busy on weekends. Purchase saffron and argan oil from certified cooperatives to ensure authenticity. The hammam session should be booked the day before. Keep some Moroccan dirhams for tips and last-minute market purchases — many vendors do not accept cards.
